history.period: Founding date UNVERIFIED - modern-era temple; temple site (trinethranarasimha.com) and local press describe it as centuries old, but no verifiable founding date or builder was found
history.summary: A Narasimha temple at Venkteshwar Nagar / Shreya Estate on Gokul Road, Hubballi, dedicated to Lakshmi Narasimha. Its distinction is the three-eyed (trinetra) idol - ordinary Narasimha idols have two eyes, but here the deity has three, like Shiva - which local press (Vijay Karnataka) calls one of India's rarest Narasimha shrines. The sanctum idol is worshipped in both Ugra Narasimha and Shanta Narasimha forms and is believed to remove devotees' suffering. The complex, set in greenery suited for meditation, also has shrines for Lakshmi, Anjaneya, Navagrahas, and Ganesha. Founding date and history are UNVERIFIED - no reliable historical sources found; treat age claims as devotional tradition.

name: Trinetra Shri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple
town_description: Hubballi (Hubli), twin city of Dharwad, is the commercial and transport hub of North Karnataka and its largest city by population. Once a 12th-century trading post under the Chalukyas, it is today a major railway and industrial centre. The temple stands in the Gokul Road area (Venkteshwar Nagar / Shreya Estate, near Silver Town), a growing residential locality of the city.

travel.road: Silver Town, Shreya Estate, Gokul Road, Venkteshwar Nagar, Hubballi 580030; easily reachable from the Hubli railway/bus station by auto or taxi
